residency.test: Resident after 183 days in any 12-month period, or 270 days in any 36-month period.
residency.worldwide_income: Yes for residents. Residence for treaty purposes can end earlier than domestic residence.
residency.paye_scheme: New foreign workers can opt into a simplified 25% flat PAYE scheme (including national insurance) on employment income up to a threshold, with no deductions and no return to file.
residency.exit_tax: Norway levies an exit tax on unrealised gains above a threshold when tax residence ends.

headline.ordinary_income: 22% flat on net income after deductions
headline.bracket_tax: trinnskatt of 1.7% to 17.5% on gross personal income, on top of the 22%
headline.wealth_tax: about 1% on net wealth above 1.76m, rising to 1.1% above 20.7m

surcharges.name: Trinnskatt (bracket tax)
surcharges.note: charged on gross personal income before deductions, unlike the 22% ordinary income tax

employee.name: Trygdeavgift (national insurance)
employee.note: no contribution below the threshold; a phase-in rule applies just above it

employer.name: Arbeidsgiveravgift
employer.note: zone-dependent - lower or zero in the far north

capital_gains.shares: effective 37.84% - the gain is grossed up by 1.72 and taxed at 22%
capital_gains.shielding_deduction: a risk-free return on the share basis (skjermingsfradrag) is exempt
capital_gains.property: exempt if you owned the home for at least 12 of the last 24 months and lived in it

quirks: The bracket tax is charged on gross personal income while the 22% is charged on net income, so deductions only reduce part of your bill.
Wealth tax is real and applies to worldwide net assets including unlisted shares. It drives a lot of financial planning and has prompted some high-net-worth emigration.

New arrivals are placed on the simplified 25% PAYE scheme by default in their first year. It is simple, but for anyone with mortgage interest or commuting costs the ordinary system is usually cheaper - the choice can be revisited.
Everything is transparent: the tax lists (skattelistene) publish income, wealth and tax paid for every taxpayer, searchable by anyone logged in with an ID.
The tax return is fully pre-filled and is treated as submitted if you do nothing, which is convenient but means unclaimed deductions are silently lost.

reporting.who_must_file: Everyone receives a pre-filled return. If it is correct you need do nothing; it is deemed submitted at the deadline. Anyone with corrections or additional income must submit changes.

deadlines.what: Pre-filled return published for the 2025 income year
Deadline to submit corrections for individuals
Deadline to request an extension, granted to 30 June
Assessments issued in batches; refunds follow
Additional payment (tilleggsforskudd) to avoid interest on underpayments

forms.name: Business income specification for the self-employed
Tax deduction card, set at the start of the year and adjustable at any time

documents_to_collect: Fødselsnummer or D-number and an electronic ID
The pre-filled return, which already includes salary, bank interest, debt and most securities
Mortgage interest statements, including for foreign mortgages which are not pre-filled
Documentation of commuting distance, home-away-from-home costs and travel for those who qualify
Foreign income and foreign tax paid for credit relief
Valuations of foreign property and unlisted shares for wealth tax

penalties.late_filing: enforcement fine (tvangsmulkt) of about 1,277 per day, capped at roughly 63,850
penalties.incorrect_information: additional tax of 20%, rising to 40-60% where the omission is intentional
penalties.interest: charged on underpaid tax from the deadline for additional advance payment

warnings: Wealth tax is not modelled and can dominate the bill for asset-rich taxpayers.
The trygdeavgift phase-in just above the threshold is simplified to a hard floor.
The simplified 25% PAYE scheme for new arrivals is not modelled; if it applies the calculation is simply 25% of gross.
